162: ### ST5: Generate Per-Meeting Folders with HTML + JSON
163: 
164: **Prose:** Split the full-chat export into per-meeting subfolders. Each subfolder gets a copy of the meeting-specific HTML and JSON from the original export.
165: 
166: **Steps:**
167: 
168: 1. Parse the JSON file (`teams-export.json`) to identify meeting boundaries.
169:     - Detect `"Meeting started"` and `"Meeting ended"` system messages from the `messageType` field.
170:     - Treat `"added <participant>"` messages as pre-meeting context (belongs to the upcoming meeting folder, not a separate meeting).
171:     - **Meeting vs false-start rule:** A `Meeting started` → `Meeting ended` pair is a real meeting ONLY if it has ≥1 participant message (chat, file share) or a non-zero duration label (`⏱ 10m` etc). A 17-second pair with 0 messages and no label is likely a false start / test. File such meetings under a `.false-starts/` subfolder instead of a `meeting-.../` subfolder. The example in this export (17-second intro with `⏱ 10m` label and 3 messages on Mar 25) IS a real meeting — the label > 0m and messages > 0 are what make it real, not the short duration.
172:

174:    ```

176:    ```

344: **Per-meeting `meeting-notes.yaml` (initial, before Phase 5 enrichment):**
345: 
346: Rich metadata per meeting:
347: - `folder_name` — meeting folder path
348: - `description` — human-readable summary
349: - `derived_from_work_log` — cross-reference to rough log (file + line + explanation)
350: - `timestamps` — UTC timestamps (from JSON) plus `duration_label`
351: - `duration_discrepancy` — ts-based vs label-based duration with delta and note
352: - `participants` — ordered list (late joiners noted via add-member events)
353: - `messages` — count of chat messages
354: - `post_meeting_chat` — structured array of post-meeting messages (speaker, time, content)
355: - `key_topics` — topic clusters from message content review
356:

379:

756: ### 7D: Verify with Existing Tools
757: 
758: The structured formatted log files can be consumed by the pre-existing scripts:
759: 
760: **Work-log file placement:** Rough logs (`<month><year>-rough.txt`) and structured logs (`<month><year>.txt`) live in the `work-logs/` directory alongside the chat folders — NOT inside any meeting folder. The path is:
761: ```
762: oleovista-acer-teams-chats/work-logs/
763:   mar2026-rough.txt
764:   mar2026.txt
765:   ...
766: ```
767: 
768: - **`convert-teams-json.py`** — alternative path for auto-generation. Reads Teams JSON from stdin, extracts `Event/Call` events (`callStarted`/`callEnded`), converts UTC→IST, and outputs formatted lines.
769: - **`analyze_time.py`** — reads structured `.txt` files, parses the `DD/MM/YYYY Day HH:MM:SS HH:MM:SS "Description"` format, computes durations, totals by day, and outputs human-readable tables with remaining-hours tracking.

894: 
895: 11. **Per-meeting folders:** Each meeting gets its own subfolder with self-contained HTML + JSON + YAML. This makes meetings linkable, independently versionable, and reviewable without cross-referencing the full export.
896: 
897: 12. **`meeting-notes.yaml` is the SSOT for each meeting:** Structured YAML is machine-parseable, diff-friendly, and cross-referenceable. It consolidates timestamps, participants, duration discrepancies, work-log cross-references, and topic clusters in one place.
898: 
899: 13. **Rough log enrichment inline:** Enrich existing rough log entries directly rather than creating separate notes — this preserves the diary's chronological flow while adding precise meeting timestamps and participant context inline.
900: 
901: 14. **Separate structured entries for reporting:** The `<month><year>.txt` format (`DD/MM/YYYY Day HH:MM:SS HH:MM:SS "Description"`) is standardized, queryable, and reporting-ready. It is consumed by `analyze_time.py` for total-hours computation and audit.
902: 
903: 15. **Timestamp format with seconds:** Use `HHMMSS` (with seconds) not `HHMM` in folder names, because the `⏱` duration label often includes seconds (e.g., `20m 38s`), and ignoring them would lose precision in the folder end time.

770: 
771: ### 7D: Verify with Existing Tools (MANDATORY)
772: 
773: Run the pre-existing scripts to verify the structured work-log entries are parseable and the formatted output is correct. This step validates timestamps, date formats, and description formatting before committing.
774: 
775: **Work-log file placement:** Rough logs (`<month><year>-rough.txt`) and structured logs (`<month><year>.txt`) live in the `work-logs/` directory alongside the chat folders — NOT inside any meeting folder. The path is:
776: ```
777: oleovista-acer-teams-chats/work-logs/
778:   mar2026-rough.txt
779:   mar2026.txt
780:   ...
781: ```
782: 
783: **Steps:**
784: 
785: 1. **`convert-teams-json.py`** — verify the structured entry format against raw JSON. This script reads Teams JSON from stdin, extracts `Event/Call` events (`callStarted`/`callEnded`), converts UTC→IST, and outputs formatted lines. Run it to confirm your hand-written structured entries match the expected format:
786:    ```bash
787:    python3 oleovista-acers/scripts/work-log/convert-teams-json.py \
788:      < oleovista-acer-teams-chats/<chat-folder>/teams-chat-exporter_<ts>/teams-export.json
789:    ```
790:    If the output format matches your `<month><year>.txt` entries, the structured log is correct.
791: 
792: 2. **`analyze_time.py`** — verify the structured `.txt` file parses correctly and computes expected durations:
793:    ```bash
794:    python3 oleovista-acers/scripts/work-log/analyze_time.py \
795:      --file oleovista-acer-teams-chats/work-logs/<month><year>.txt
796:    ```
797:    If it parses without errors and shows reasonable totals, the structured log is valid.
798: 
799: 3. Fix any parsing errors (wrong date format, missing time fields, malformed description) before committing.
800:

813: ```
814: 
815: This groups all related files — exporter data, meeting folders, work-log entries — into one atomic unit. Preferred when the export involves one meeting or a small, cohesive set of changes.

818:

868: # Skill: git-atomic-commit-construction
869: 
870: # Git Atomic Commit Construction Skill
871: 
872: > **Skill ID:** `git-atomic-commit-construction`
873: > **Version:** 1.0.0
874: > **Standard:** [Agent Skills (agentskills.io)](https://agentskills.io)
875: 
876: ## Description
877: 
878: Construct high-quality, atomic Git commits from a set of working-tree
879: changes. This skill covers the full lifecycle: environment validation,
880: change analysis, logical grouping, hunk-based staging, formatting
881: isolation, commit message quality, execution with user authorization,
882: and post-commit verification.
883: 
884: Every commit produced by this skill is independent, logically coherent,
885: and buildable. Mixed concerns are never committed together. Formatting
886: is separated from logic. Configuration is coupled to its functional
887: change. The user retains full control via mandatory preview and explicit
888: "start" authorization.
889: 
890: ## Source Rules
891: 
892: This skill distills and operationalizes the following rule files:
893: 
894: | Rule File | Scope Incorporated |
895: |---|---|
896: | [`git-atomic-commit-construction-rules.md`](../../../ai-agent-rules/git-atomic-commit-construction-rules.md) | All 15 phases (primary source) |
897: | [`git-operation-rules.md`](../../../ai-agent-rules/git-operation-rules.md) | Phase -1, 0, 1 (environment, repo context, change detection) and Sections 2–4 (commit/push/stash protocols) |
898: 
899: For history refinement (splitting existing commits), see the
900: [`git_history_refinement`](../git-history-refinement/SKILL.md) skill.
901: For complex multi-branch rebasing, see the
902: [`git_rebase`](../git-rebase-standardization/SKILL.md) skill.
903: 
904: ## Prerequisites
905: 
906: | Requirement | Minimum |
907: |---|---|
908: | VCS | Git 2.x+ |
909: | Shell | PowerShell 5.1+ or Bash 4+ |
910: | Access | Write access to the project repository |
911: | Auth | GitHub CLI authenticated (if pushing to GitHub) |
912: 
913: ## When to Apply
914: 
915: Apply this skill when:
916: 
917: - A user asks to "commit changes," "arrange commits," or "stage and commit"
918: - `git status` shows staged, unstaged, or untracked modifications
919: - Multiple unrelated changes exist in the working tree and need separation
920: - A user asks to review what should be committed
921: - **After ANY submodule commit is executed, the skill AUTOMATICALLY checks for
922:   and offers the parent repository submodule SHA update (if applicable) and
923:   executes it upon user "yes" — no separate user request needed**
924: 
925: Do NOT apply when:
926: 
927: - The user asks to refine or split **existing** commits — use
928:   [`git_history_refinement`](../git-history-refinement/SKILL.md) instead
929: - The user asks to rebase branches — use
930:   [`git_rebase`](../git-rebase-standardization/SKILL.md) instead
931: - The request is a simple single-file, single-concern commit with no
932:   mixed changes (a lightweight commit suffices without the full protocol)
933: - The files being committed are **personal-only** and should NOT reach the
934:   team's `origin` — route the commit to a personal sandbox branch via
935:   [`git-personal-sandbox-remote`](../git-personal-sandbox-remote/SKILL.md)
936:   (this skill still applies to the commit itself, but the destination
937:   remote/branch changes)
938: 
939: **Push Policy (GLOBAL)**: The agent MUST NEVER execute `git push` automatically.
940: After any commit(s), the agent MAY OFFER to push (e.g., "Push to remote?") but
941: MUST WAIT for explicit user approval. Only push when the user explicitly says
942: "yes", "push", or issues a direct `git push` command. No exceptions.
943: 
944: ---
945: 
946: ## Step-by-Step Procedure
947: 
948: ### Step 0 — Environment & Repository Context
949: 
950: Before any Git commands, validate the environment and establish context.
951: 
952: #### 0a — Authenticate Services
953: 
954: Verify authentication for required services:
955: 
956: ```powershell
957: gh auth status        # GitHub CLI
958: ```
959: 
960: If authentication is missing, guide the user through login.
961: 
962: #### 0b — Identify the Target Repository
963: 
964: Determine the correct repository from the user's request and file paths.
965: 
966: - **Nested repositories:** If changes are in a sub-directory that is its
967:   own Git project, use `PAGER=cat git -C` to execute `PAGER=cat git` commands in that repository.
968: - **Ambiguity:** If multiple repositories exist in the workspace and the
969:   target is unclear, ask the user for clarification.
970: 
971: #### 0c — Working Directory Persistence (Critical)
972: 
973: When working with `git` commands, use `git -C <path>` for reliable directory targeting:
974: 
975: ```powershell
976: # Recommended: git -C with absolute path
977: git -C /path/to/repo status
978: git -C /path/to/repo diff HEAD
979: 
980: # Why this matters: Shell `cd` commands do not persist across tool invocations
981: # in stateless execution environments. Using git -C ensures consistent behavior
982: # across all command chains and multi-step workflows.
983: 
984: # Pattern for multi-repo work:

The pipeline is designed to be applied to any other Teams meeting export file.

11620: 108:      anjitha-dileena-muhammed-3_2026-03-25_2026-07-04/

11622: 110: 
11623: 111: ### ST3: Unzip
11624: 112: 
11625: 113: **Steps:**
11626: 114: 
11627: 115: 1. Unzip inside the chat folder:

11633: 121: 
11634: 122: ### ST4: Rename the Export Folder and Files
11635: 123: 
11636: 124: **Goals:**
11637: 125: 1. Rename extracted files to generic `teams-export.<ext>`.
11638: 126: 2. Stamp the exporter generation timestamp onto the parent folder name.
11639: 127: 3. Handle the message extractor output.
11640: 128: 
11641: 129: **Steps:**
11642: 130: 
11643: 131: 1. Move the 5 exported files (CSV, HTML, JSON, PDF, TXT) out of the nested inner folder into the export folder. Remove the empty inner folder.
11644: 132: 
11645: 133: 2. Rename the 5 files to bare `teams-export.<ext>`:
11646: 134:    ```bash
11647: 135:    mv TeamsExport_<title>_<ts>.csv teams-export.csv

11651: 139:    mv TeamsExport_<title>_<ts>.txt teams-export.txt
11652: 140:    ```
11653: 141: 
11654: 142: 3. Rename the export parent folder to include the generation timestamp:
11655: 143:    ```
11656: 144:    teams-chat-exporter_<YYYY-MM-DD>_<HHMMSS>
11657: 145:    ```
11658: 146:    Example: `teams-export-qa-frontend-meeting-2026-07-18-18-49-51` → `teams-chat-exporter_2026-07-18_184951`
11659: 147: 
11660: 148: 4. Move message extractor files (`.csv`, `.html`, `.md`) into a `teams-message-extractor-chat-export/` subfolder inside the chat folder. These files from the message extractor generator sit alongside — not inside — the exporter folder.
11661: 149: 
11662: 150: 5. Remove the original ZIP (it is already extracted).
11663: 151: 
11664: 152: **Resulting structure — raw files directly in the timestamped exporter folder:**
11665: 153: ```
11666: 154: <chat-folder>/
11667: 155:   teams-chat-exporter_<timestamp>/     ← exporter + timestamp
11668: 156:     teams-export.{csv,html,json,pdf,txt}
11669: 157:     meeting-.../                       ← added in ST5/ST6
11670: 158:   teams-message-extractor-chat-export/
11671: 159:     teams-messages-<date>.{csv,html,md}
11672: 160: ```
11673: 161: 
11674: 162: ### ST5: Generate Per-Meeting Folders with HTML + JSON
11675: 163: 
11676: 164: **Prose:** Split the full-chat export into per-meeting subfolders. Each subfolder gets a copy of the meeting-specific HTML and JSON from the original export.
11677: 165: 
11678: 166: **Steps:**
11679: 167: 
11680: 168: 1. Parse the JSON file (`teams-export.json`) to identify meeting boundaries.
11681: 169:     - Detect `"Meeting started"` and `"Meeting ended"` system messages from the `messageType` field.
11682: 170:     - Treat `"added <participant>"` messages as pre-meeting context (belongs to the upcoming meeting folder, not a separate meeting).
11683: 171:     - **Meeting vs false-start rule:** A `Meeting started` → `Meeting ended` pair is a real meeting ONLY if it has ≥1 participant message (chat, file share) or a non-zero duration label (`⏱ 10m` etc). A 17-second pair with 0 messages and no label is likely a false start / test. File such meetings under a `.false-starts/` subfolder instead of a `meeting-.../` subfolder. The example in this export (17-second intro with `⏱ 10m` label and 3 messages on Mar 25) IS a real meeting — the label > 0m and messages > 0 are what make it real, not the short duration.
11684: 172: 
11685: 173: 2. For each meeting detected, create a subfolder named:
11686: 174:    ```
11687: 175:    meeting-<YYYY-MM-DD>_<IST-start-HHMMSS>_<IST-end-HHMMSS>-<topic>/
11688: 176:    ```
11689: 177: 
11690: 178: 3. Extract the messages for that meeting from the JSON and write a partial JSON file into the meeting subfolder.
11691: 179: 
11692: 180: **Timestamp computation rules:**
11693: 181: 
11694: 182: - All timestamps in the export are in **UTC** (e.g., `2026-03-25T07:18:11.973Z`).
11695: 183: - Convert to **IST** (+5:30) for folder naming.
11696: 184: - The meeting date used in the folder name is the **IST date** of the meeting start (this matters when meetings start before midnight UTC and span into the next IST day).
11697: 185: - Initial format: `HHMM` (hours+minutes). Later refined to `HHMMSS` (with seconds) in Phase 4.
11698: 186: 
11699: 187: **Duration handling:**
11700: 188: 
11701: 189: - The Teams Chat Exporter places a `⏱ <duration>` label on the "Meeting ended" divider (e.g., `⏱ 10m`, `⏱ 20m 38s`, `⏱ 6h 2m 39s`).
11702: 190: - This label often **differs** from the actual `Meeting started → Meeting ended` timestamp span.
11703: 191: - Initial approach: use the label-based end time as the folder end time (it's always greater).
11704: 192: - **Final rule (ST7):** Folder end time = `max(meeting-ended-timestamp, start + duration-label)`.
11705: 193: 
11706: 194: ### ST6: Split Original HTML at Meeting Boundaries
11707: 195: 
11708: 196: **IMPORTANT REFINEMENT:** The initial approach split meetings by generating partial HTML from JSON. This produced minimal HTML missing the rich content (embedded images, proper CSS, participant avatars, divider styling). The session then switched to **splitting the original HTML file** at meeting boundaries.
11709: 197: 
11710: 198: **HTML structure overview:**
11711: 199: 
11712: 200: The Teams Chat Exporter HTML has this overall structure:
11713: 201: ```html
11714: 202: <html>
11715: 203:   <head>
11716: 204:     <style>...</style>        <!-- CSS for the entire export -->
11717: 205:     <script>...</script>      <!-- compact-view toggle, image modal -->
11718: 206:   </head>
11719: 207:   <body>
11720: 208:     <div id="wrapper">
11721: 209:       <div id="header-row">...</div>         <!-- global header (title, counts) -->
11722: 210:       <div id="export-body">
11723: 211:         <div class="divider-block">          <!-- Meeting started -->
11724: 212:           <div class="divider-left">
11725: 213:             <div class="msg-from">Meeting started</div>
11726: 214:             <div class="msg-timestamp" datetime="2026-...">...</div>
11727: 215:           </div>
11728: 216:         </div>
11729: 217:         ... message rows ...
11730: 218:         <div class="divider-block">          <!-- Meeting ended -->
11731: 219:           <div class="divider-left">
11732: 220:             <span class="msg-timestamp" datetime="...">⏱ 10m</span>
11733: 221:             <div class="msg-from">Meeting ended</div>
11734: 222:           </div>
11735: 223:         </div>
11736: 224:         ... post-meeting messages ...
11737: 225:         <div class="divider-block">          <!-- next Meeting started -->
11738: 226:           ...
11739: 227:         </div>
11740: 228:       </div>
11741: 229:     </div>
11742: 230:   </body>
11743: 231: </html>
11744: 232: ```
11745: 233: 
11746: 234: **Divider block closing pattern varies by export version.** The closing `</div>` count after a `<div class="divider-block">` depends on nesting depth. Instead of counting closing tags, use a split-on-content approach (see script below).
11747: 235: 
11748: 236: **Steps:**
11749: 237: 
11750: 238: 1. **Split HTML by meeting boundaries** using a pattern-matching script (not hardcoded byte offsets which break on different exports):
11751: 239: 
11752: 240:    ```bash
11753: 241:    python3 <<'PYEOF'
11754: 242:    import re, os, json
11755: 243:    from datetime import datetime, timezone, timedelta
11756: 244: 
11757: 245:    IST = timezone(timedelta(hours=5, minutes=30))
11758: 246:    LATEST_FOLDER = None  # set to latest exporter folder
11759: 247: 
11760: 248:    def parse_meetings(html):
11761: 249:        # Find every divider block
11762: 250:        dividers = list(re.finditer(
11763: 251:            r'<div class="divider-block">(.*?)</div>\s*</div>\s*</div>',
11764: 252:            html, re.DOTALL
11765: 253:        ))
11766: 254:        meetings = []
11767: 255:        for i, m in enumerate(dividers):
11768: 256:            block = m.group()
11769: 257:            if 'Meeting started' in block:
11770: 258:                start_idx = m.start()
11771: 259:                # Find the next Meeting ended divider
11772: 260:                for j in range(i+1, len(dividers)):
11773: 261:                    if 'Meeting ended' in dividers[j].group():
11774: 262:                        end_idx = dividers[j].end()
11775: 263:                        segment = html[start_idx:end_idx]
11776: 264:                        meetings.append((segment, m.start(), dividers[j].end()))
11777: 265:                        break
11778: 266:        return meetings
11779: 267: 
11780: 268:    # Load preamble (everything before first divider-block)
11781: 269:    preamble_end = html.find('<div class="divider-block">')
11782: 270:    before = html[:preamble_end]
11783: 271: 
11784: 272:    # Split into per-meeting files
11785: 273:    for i, (segment, start_off, end_off) in enumerate(parse_meetings(html)):
11786: 274:        # Determine meeting folder name from segment
11787: 275:        name_match = re.search(r'class="msg-from">(.+?)</div>', segment[:500])
11788: 276:        if name_match:
11789: 277:            topic = name_match.group(1).strip().lower().replace(' ', '-')
11790: 278:        else:
11791: 279:            topic = f"meeting-{i+1}"
11792: 280:        # Write per-meeting HTML with same preamble
11793: 281:        with open(f"meetings/{topic}/teams-export.html", 'w') as f:
11794: 282:            f.write(before + segment + '\n</div></div></body></html>\n')
11795: 283:    PYEOF
11796: 284:    ```
11797: 285: 
11798: 286: 2. **Filter JSON per meeting.** The full `teams-export.json` contains all meetings concatenated. For each meeting, extract only the JSON messages whose `timestamp` falls between the meeting's start and end:
11799: 287: 
11800: 288:    ```bash
11801: 289:    python3 <<'PYEOF'
11802: 290:    import json
11803: 291:    from datetime import datetime
11804: 292: 
11805: 293:    with open('teams-export.json') as f:
11806: 294:        data = json.load(f)
11807: 295: 
11808: 296:    meetings = [...]  # from ST5 meeting detection
11809: 297:    for m in meetings:
11810: 298:        start_utc = m['start_ts']
11811: 299:        end_utc   = m['end_ts']
11812: 300:        filtered = [
11813: 301:            msg for msg in data
11814: 302:            if msg.get('timestamp', '').startswith(start_utc[:10])
11815: 303:            and start_utc <= msg['timestamp'] <= end_utc
11816: 304:        ]
11817: 305:        with open(f"meetings/{m['folder']}/teams-export.json", 'w') as f:
11818: 306:            json.dump(filtered, f, indent=2)
11819: 307:    PYEOF
11820: 308:    ```
11821: 309: 
11822: 310: 3. **Fix per-meeting HTML metadata.** After splitting, the HTML header still shows the global export counts (total participants, total messages). Update the `#header-row` section in each per-meeting HTML to reflect only that meeting's data:
11823: 311:    - Participant count → distinct participants within the meeting window
11824: 312:    - Message count → filtered JSON message count
11825: 313:    - Date range → meeting start–end dates
11826: 314:    - Title → meeting topic from folder name
11827: 315: 
11828: 316: 4. Write the resulting per-meeting HTML to `<meeting-folder>/teams-export.html`.
11829: 317: 
11830: 318: 5. Write the per-meeting JSON to `<meeting-folder>/teams-export.json`.
11831: 319: 
11832: 320: **Key detail:** The HTML preamble includes embedded CSS styles and a `<script>` block for the compact-view toggle and image modal. These must be preserved in each per-meeting HTML for the file to render correctly standalone.
11833: 321: 
11834: 322: ### ST7: Duration-Label vs Timestamp-Span Correction
11835: 323: 
11836: 324: **Prose:** Correct meeting folder end times to use the greater of the two possible end times.
11837: 325: 
11838: 326: **Steps:**
11839: 327: 
11840: 328: 1. For each meeting, compute two end times:
11841: 329:    - **Timestamp-based:** `Meeting ended` UTC timestamp → IST.
11842: 330:    - **Label-based:** `Meeting started` UTC + `⏱ <duration>` label → IST.
11843: 331: 
11844: 332: 2. Use `max(ts_based, label_based)` as the folder end time.
11845: 333: 
11846: 334: 3. Document the discrepancy in a per-meeting `meeting-notes.yaml` file.
11847: 335: 
11848: 336: **Example discrepancies for the 3 meetings in this export:**
11849: 337: 
11850: 338: | Meeting | TS Span | Label Duration | Delta | Folder End Uses |
11851: 339: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
11852: 340: | Mar 25 intro | 1m 56s | 10m | +8m 04s | Label (10m) |
11853: 341: | May 7 sync | 17m 08s | 20m 38s | +3m 30s | Label (20m38s) |
11854: 342: | Jul 4 staging | 5h 56m 35s | 6h 2m 39s | +6m 04s | Label (6h2m39s) |
11855: 343: 
11856: 344: **Per-meeting `meeting-notes.yaml` (initial, before Phase 5 enrichment):**
11857: 345: 
11858: 346: Rich metadata per meeting:
11859: 347: - `folder_name` — meeting folder path
11860: 348: - `description` — human-readable summary
11861: 349: - `derived_from_work_log` — cross-reference to rough log (file + line + explanation)
11862: 350: - `timestamps` — UTC timestamps (from JSON) plus `duration_label`
11863: 351: - `duration_discrepancy` — ts-based vs label-based duration with delta and note
11864: 352: - `participants` — ordered list (late joiners noted via add-member events)
11865: 353: - `messages` — count of chat messages
11866: 354: - `post_meeting_chat` — structured array of post-meeting messages (speaker, time, content)
11867: 355: - `key_topics` — topic clusters from message content review
11868: 356: 
11869: 357: **Template:**
11870: 358: ```yaml
11871: 359: folder_name: meeting-<date>_<start-HHMMSS>_<end-HHMMSS>-<topic>
11872: 360: description: "<summary>"
11873: 361: derived_from_work_log: |
11874: 362:   <file> line <N>:
11875: 363:   "<excerpt>"

11877: 365: 
11878: 366: timestamps:
11879: 367:   meeting_started_utc: "<ISO-8601>"
11880: 368:   meeting_ended_utc: "<ISO-8601>"
11881: 369:   duration_label: "<⏱ value>"
11882: 370: 
11883: 371: duration_discrepancy:
11884: 372:   ts_based: "<H:MM:SS>"
11885: 373:   label_based: "<H:MM:SS>"
11886: 374:   delta: "<H:MM:SS>"
11887: 375:   note: >
11888: 376:     The "⏱ <duration>" label on "Meeting ended" is <delta> longer than the
11889: 377:     actual Meeting started → Meeting ended timestamp span. Folder end time
11890: 378:     uses the greater value (label-based).
11891: 379: 
11892: 380: participants:
11893: 381:   - <name1>
11894: 382:   - <name2>
11895: 383: 
11896: 384: messages: <count>
11897: 385: 
11898: 386: post_meeting_chat:
11899: 387:   entries:
11900: 388:     - speaker: <name>
11901: 389:       time_ist: "<HH:MM>"

11903: 391:   note: "<context>"
11904: 392: 
11905: 393: key_topics:
11906: 394:   - description: "<brief label>"
11907: 395:     detail: "<elaboration or context>"
11908: 396:   - description: "<brief label>"
11909: 397:     detail: "<elaboration or context>"
11910: 398: ```

12001: 489: ## Phase 3: Analyze a Particular Meeting
12002: 490: 
12003: 491: **Prose:** Deep analysis of a specific meeting's HTML content, checking whether the meeting title aligns with the actual chat content.
12004: 492: 
12005: 493: **Steps:**
12006: 494: 
12007: 495: 1. Open the per-meeting HTML file (`teams-export.html`) for the chosen meeting.
12008: 496: 2. Review all messages, attachments, and system events:
12009: 497:    - Message content (text, code snippets)
12010: 498:    - Attachments (files shared, URLs)
12011: 499:    - Participant list and add-member events
12012: 500:    - Duration and recording info
12013: 501: 3. Compare the meeting title against the actual content.
12014: 502: 4. Identify topic clusters present in the conversation.
12015: 503: 
12016: 504: **Example (Jul 4 meeting):** The HTML review revealed 3 distinct topic clusters that the original title `local-testing-environment-setup-for-praveena-razik` did not fully cover:
12017: 505:    1. Local testing env setup — .env files, backend/frontend env URLs
12018: 506:    2. Staging DB dump — SQL dump shared by Dileena, forwarded to Praveena & Razik
12019: 507:    3. API trade processing script — Python code for `API_Pending_Trades` reconciliation
12020: 508: 
12021: 509: This analysis feeds directly into Phase 5 (meeting naming from work logs). The final title was chosen to cover all clusters: `local-testing-env-setup-and-staging-data-reconciliation`.
12022: 510: 
12023: 511: ---
12024: 512: 
12025: 513: ## Phase 4: Add Seconds to Folder Timestamps
12026: 514: 
12027: 515: **Prose:** The user requested that folder timestamp portions use `HHMMSS` (with seconds) instead of `HHMM`.
12028: 516: 
12029: 517: **Steps:**
12030: 518: 
12031: 519: 1. For each meeting, compute precise IST start and end times including seconds using Python:
12032: 520:    ```python
12033: 521:    from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
12034: 522: 
12035: 523:    start_utc = datetime.strptime(start_utc_str.replace('Z','').split('.')[0],
12036: 524:                                  '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S').replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
12037: 525:    h, m, s = [int(x) for x in dur_str.split(':')]
12038: 526:    dur = timedelta(hours=h, minutes=m, seconds=s)
12039: 527:    end_by_dur = start_utc + dur
12040: 528: 
12041: 529:    def fmt_ist(dt):
12042: 530:        ist = dt.astimezone(timezone(timedelta(hours=5, minutes=30)))
12043: 531:        return ist.strftime('%H%M%S')
12044: 532: 
12045: 533:    start_ist = fmt_ist(start_utc)
12046: 534:    end_ist = fmt_ist(end_by_dur)
12047: 535:    date = start_utc.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
12048: 536:    new_folder = f"meeting-{date}_{start_ist}_{end_ist}-{topic}"
12049: 537:    ```
12050: 538: 
12051: 539: 2. Rename folders to include seconds:
12052: 540:    ```
12053: 541:    HHMM → HHMMSS
12054: 542:    ```
12055: 543: 
12056: 544: 3. Update all references — `meeting-notes.yaml` folder_name fields.
12057: 545: 
12058: 546: **Example:**
12059: 547: ```
12060: 548: meeting-2026-03-25_1248_1258-intro
12061: 549:     → meeting-2026-03-25_124811_125811-intro
12062: 550: ```
12063: 551: IST start: 07:18:11 UTC + 5:30 = 12:48:11 — seconds (11) now included.
12064: 552: 
12065: 553: **Result:**
12066: 554: ```
12067: 555: meeting-2026-03-25_124811_125811-intro
12068: 556: meeting-2026-05-07_121730_123808-sync
12069: 557: meeting-2026-07-04_152232_212511-staging-deployment-api-optimization-env-setup
12070: 558: ```

12358: 846:    └─ write meeting-notes.yaml with work_log_ref
12359: 847:

12361: 849:     └─ <slug>_<date1>_<date2>_<date3> (not range)
12362: 850: 
12363: 851: 11. ENRICH WORK LOGS (Phase 7)
12364: 852:     ├─ rough logs: add meeting details to existing day entries
12365: 853:     ├─ rough logs: create new month file if missing (e.g. jul2026-rough.txt)
12366: 854:     └─ structured logs: create <month><year>.txt with formatted entries

12385: 873: ## Key Decisions and Gotchas
12386: 874: 
12387: 875: 1. **Symlink is a prerequisite, not a workflow step.** The symlink was completed before the session. If files are already in git or placed manually, skip it entirely.
12388: 876: 
12389: 877: 2. **Timestamp source:** Export filenames contain export-generation timestamps, NOT meeting dates. Actual meeting dates come ONLY from JSON `timestamp` fields or HTML `datetime` attributes.
12390: 878: 
12391: 879: 3. **UTC → IST conversion:** All meeting times are UTC in the export. Convert to IST (+5:30) for folder names and work-log entries. The folder date must be the IST date, not the UTC date.
12392: 880: 
12393: 881: 4. **Duration-label discrepancy:** The `⏱` label on "Meeting ended" system divider differs from the actual `Meeting started → Meeting ended` timestamp span in every meeting. Always use `max(ts-span, label)`. Document the delta in `meeting-notes.yaml`.
12394: 882: 
12395: 883: 5. **HTML splitting vs JSON generation:** Generating per-meeting HTML from JSON produces incomplete HTML (missing embedded images, CSS, participant avatars). Always split the ORIGINAL HTML at meeting boundary markers, preserving the `<style>` and `<script>` preamble blocks from the full HTML file.
12396: 884: 
12397: 885: 6. **Add-member messages:** System messages like `"X added Y"` that appear before `"Meeting started"` are pre-meeting context. They belong to the meeting folder (not a separate meeting). Include these participants in the meeting's participant list with a note that they joined after the meeting start.
12398: 886: 
12399: 887: 7. **Meeting naming:** Never rely on AI-generated assumptions. Cross-reference with existing rough work logs by date, time window, and participant match. If no work-log entry exists, name based on actual message content reviewed in the per-meeting HTML. The user may provide context (as they did for the Jul 4 meeting).
12400: 888: 
12401: 889: 8. **Folder name format:** The chat-level folder should list discrete meeting dates, not a range. Timestamps include seconds (`HHMMSS`). The exporter-generation timestamp lives in the generator subfolder name, not in every file.
12402: 890: 
12403: 891: 9. **Two work-log formats coexist:** Rough (`*rough.txt`) is freeform diary. Structured (`<month><year>.txt`) is one-line-per-entry with exact timestamps. Both must be updated for each meeting. The structured format is consumable by `analyze_time.py`.
12404: 892: 
12405: 893: 10. **Existing tools:** `convert-teams-json.py` auto-generates structured entries from JSON. `analyze_time.py` computes totals from structured files. Use these as verification/complementary steps, not as the primary pipeline.
12406: 894: 
12407: 895: 11. **Per-meeting folders:** Each meeting gets its own subfolder with self-contained HTML + JSON + YAML. This makes meetings linkable, independently versionable, and reviewable without cross-referencing the full export.
12408: 896: 
12409: 897: 12. **`meeting-notes.yaml` is the SSOT for each meeting:** Structured YAML is machine-parseable, diff-friendly, and cross-referenceable. It consolidates timestamps, participants, duration discrepancies, work-log cross-references, and topic clusters in one place.
12410: 898: 
12411: 899: 13. **Rough log enrichment inline:** Enrich existing rough log entries directly rather than creating separate notes — this preserves the diary's chronological flow while adding precise meeting timestamps and participant context inline.
12412: 900:

13268: 162: ### ST5: Generate Per-Meeting Folders with HTML + JSON
13269: 163: 
13270: 164: **Prose:** Split the full-chat export into per-meeting subfolders. Each subfolder gets a copy of the meeting-specific HTML and JSON from the original export.
13271: 165: 
13272: 166: **Steps:**
13273: 167: 
13274: 168: 1. Parse the JSON file (`teams-export.json`) to identify meeting boundaries.
13275: 169:     - Detect `"Meeting started"` and `"Meeting ended"` system messages from the `messageType` field.
13276: 170:     - Treat `"added <participant>"` messages as pre-meeting context (belongs to the upcoming meeting folder, not a separate meeting).
13277: 171:     - **Meeting vs false-start rule:** A `Meeting started` → `Meeting ended` pair is a real meeting ONLY if it has ≥1 participant message (chat, file share) or a non-zero duration label (`⏱ 10m` etc). A 17-second pair with 0 messages and no label is likely a false start / test. File such meetings under a `.false-starts/` subfolder instead of a `meeting-.../` subfolder. The example in this export (17-second intro with `⏱ 10m` label and 3 messages on Mar 25) IS a real meeting — the label > 0m and messages > 0 are what make it real, not the short duration.

13279: 173: 2. For each meeting detected, create a subfolder named:
13280: 174:    ```
13281: 175:    meeting-<YYYY-MM-DD>_<IST-start-HHMMSS>_<IST-end-HHMMSS>-<topic>/
13282: 176:    ```

13426: 756: ### 7D: Verify with Existing Tools
13427: 757: 
13428: 758: The structured formatted log files can be consumed by the pre-existing scripts:
13429: 759: 
13430: 760: **Work-log file placement:** Rough logs (`<month><year>-rough.txt`) and structured logs (`<month><year>.txt`) live in the `work-logs/` directory alongside the chat folders — NOT inside any meeting folder. The path is:
13431: 761: ```
13432: 762: oleovista-acer-teams-chats/work-logs/
13433: 763:   mar2026-rough.txt
13434: 764:   mar2026.txt
13435: 765:   ...
13436: 766: ```
13437: 767: 
13438: 768: - **`convert-teams-json.py`** — alternative path for auto-generation. Reads Teams JSON from stdin, extracts `Event/Call` events (`callStarted`/`callEnded`), converts UTC→IST, and outputs formatted lines.
13439: 769: - **`analyze_time.py`** — reads structured `.txt` files, parses the `DD/MM/YYYY Day HH:MM:SS HH:MM:SS "Description"` format, computes durations, totals by day, and outputs human-readable tables with remaining-hours tracking.

13443: 773: ## Git Commit Strategy
13444: 774: 
13445: 775: After all pipeline phases complete, commit the results atomically. Each logical unit gets its own commit:
13446: 776: 
13447: 777: | # | Commit | Scope |
13448: 778: |---|--------|-------|
13449: 779: | 1 | `feat(work-log): enrich mar2026-rough.txt with Mar 25 meeting` | rough log |
13450: 780: | 2 | `feat(work-log): enrich may2026-rough.txt with May 7 meeting` | rough log |
13451: 781: | 3 | `feat(work-log): add mar2026.txt formatted entry` | formatted |
13452: 782: | 4 | `feat(work-log): add may2026.txt formatted entry` | formatted |

13491: 898: 
13492: 899: 13. **Rough log enrichment inline:** Enrich existing rough log entries directly rather than creating separate notes — this preserves the diary's chronological flow while adding precise meeting timestamps and participant context inline.
13493: 900: 
13494: 901: 14. **Separate structured entries for reporting:** The `<month><year>.txt` format (`DD/MM/YYYY Day HH:MM:SS HH:MM:SS "Description"`) is standardized, queryable, and reporting-ready. It is consumed by `analyze_time.py` for total-hours computation and audit.
13495: 902: 
13496: 903: 15. **Timestamp format with seconds:** Use `HHMMSS` (with seconds) not `HHMM` in folder names, because the `⏱` duration label often includes seconds (e.g., `20m 38s`), and ignoring them would lose precision in the folder end time.

4415: 162: ### ST5: Generate Per-Meeting Folders with HTML + JSON
4416: 163: 
4417: 164: **Prose:** Split the full-chat export into per-meeting subfolders. Each subfolder gets a copy of the meeting-specific HTML and JSON from the original export.
4418: 165: 
4419: 166: **Steps:**
4420: 167: 
4421: 168: 1. Parse the JSON file (`teams-export.json`) to identify meeting boundaries.
4422: 169:     - Detect `"Meeting started"` and `"Meeting ended"` system messages from the `messageType` field.
4423: 170:     - Treat `"added <participant>"` messages as pre-meeting context (belongs to the upcoming meeting folder, not a separate meeting).
4424: 171:     - **Meeting vs false-start rule:** A `Meeting started` → `Meeting ended` pair is a real meeting ONLY if it has ≥1 participant message (chat, file share) or a non-zero duration label (`⏱ 10m` etc). A 17-second pair with 0 messages and no label is likely a false start / test. File such meetings under a `.false-starts/` subfolder instead of a `meeting-.../` subfolder. The example in this export (17-second intro with `⏱ 10m` label and 3 messages on Mar 25) IS a real meeting — the label > 0m and messages > 0 are what make it real, not the short duration.
4425: 172: 
4426: 173: 2. For each meeting detected, create a subfolder named:
4427: 174:    ```
4428: 175:    meeting-<YYYY-MM-DD>_<IST-start-HHMMSS>_<IST-end-HHMMSS>-<topic>/
4429: 176:    ```
4430: 177: 
4431: 178: 3. Extract the messages for that meeting from the JSON and write a partial JSON file into the meeting subfolder.
4432: 179: 
4433: 180: **Timestamp computation rules:**
4434: 181: 
4435: 182: - All timestamps in the export are in **UTC** (e.g., `2026-03-25T07:18:11.973Z`).
4436: 183: - Convert to **IST** (+5:30) for folder naming.
4437: 184: - The meeting date used in the folder name is the **IST date** of the meeting start (this matters when meetings start before midnight UTC and span into the next IST day).
4438: 185: - Initial format: `HHMM` (hours+minutes). Later refined to `HHMMSS` (with seconds) in Phase 4.
4439: 186: 
4440: 187: **Duration handling:**
4441: 188: 
4442: 189: - The Teams Chat Exporter places a `⏱ <duration>` label on the "Meeting ended" divider (e.g., `⏱ 10m`, `⏱ 20m 38s`, `⏱ 6h 2m 39s`).
4443: 190: - This label often **differs** from the actual `Meeting started → Meeting ended` timestamp span.
4444: 191: - Initial approach: use the label-based end time as the folder end time (it's always greater).
4445: 192: - **Final rule (ST7):** Folder end time = `max(meeting-ended-timestamp, start + duration-label)`.
4446: 193: 
4447: 194: ### ST6: Split Original HTML at Meeting Boundaries
4448: 195: 
4449: 196: **IMPORTANT REFINEMENT:** The initial approach split meetings by generating partial HTML from JSON. This produced minimal HTML missing the rich content (embedded images, proper CSS, participant avatars, divider styling). The session then switched to **splitting the original HTML file** at meeting boundaries.
4450: 197: 
4451: 198: **HTML structure overview:**
4452: 199: 
4453: 200: The Teams Chat Exporter HTML has this overall structure:
4454: 201: ```html
4455: 202: <html>
4456: 203:   <head>
4457: 204:     <style>...</style>        <!-- CSS for the entire export -->
4458: 205:     <script>...</script>      <!-- compact-view toggle, image modal -->
4459: 206:   </head>
4460: 207:   <body>
4461: 208:     <div id="wrapper">
4462: 209:       <div id="header-row">...</div>         <!-- global header (title, counts) -->
4463: 210:       <div id="export-body">
4464: 211:         <div class="divider-block">          <!-- Meeting started -->
4465: 212:           <div class="divider-left">
4466: 213:             <div class="msg-from">Meeting started</div>
4467: 214:             <div class="msg-timestamp" datetime="2026-...">...</div>
4468: 215:           </div>
4469: 216:         </div>
4470: 217:         ... message rows ...
4471: 218:         <div class="divider-block">          <!-- Meeting ended -->
4472: 219:           <div class="divider-left">
4473: 220:             <span class="msg-timestamp" datetime="...">⏱ 10m</span>
4474: 221:             <div class="msg-from">Meeting ended</div>
4475: 222:           </div>
4476: 223:         </div>
4477: 224:         ... post-meeting messages ...
4478: 225:         <div class="divider-block">          <!-- next Meeting started -->
4479: 226:           ...
4480: 227:         </div>
4481: 228:       </div>
4482: 229:     </div>
4483: 230:   </body>
4484: 231: </html>
4485: 232: ```
4486: 233: 
4487: 234: **Divider block closing pattern varies by export version.** The closing `</div>` count after a `<div class="divider-block">` depends on nesting depth. Instead of counting closing tags, use a split-on-content approach (see script below).
4488: 235: 
4489: 236: **Steps:**
4490: 237: 
4491: 238: 1. **Split HTML by meeting boundaries** using a pattern-matching script (not hardcoded byte offsets which break on different exports):
4492: 239: 
4493: 240:    ```bash
4494: 241:    python3 <<'PYEOF'
4495: 242:    import re, os, json
4496: 243:    from datetime import datetime, timezone, timedelta
4497: 244: 
4498: 245:    IST = timezone(timedelta(hours=5, minutes=30))
4499: 246:    LATEST_FOLDER = None  # set to latest exporter folder
4500: 247: 
4501: 248:    def parse_meetings(html):
4502: 249:        # Find every divider block
4503: 250:        dividers = list(re.finditer(
4504: 251:            r'<div class="divider-block">(.*?)</div>\s*</div>\s*</div>',
4505: 252:            html, re.DOTALL
4506: 253:        ))
4507: 254:        meetings = []
4508: 255:        for i, m in enumerate(dividers):
4509: 256:            block = m.group()
4510: 257:            if 'Meeting started' in block:
4511: 258:                start_idx = m.start()
4512: 259:                # Find the next Meeting ended divider
4513: 260:                for j in range(i+1, len(dividers)):
4514: 261:                    if 'Meeting ended' in dividers[j].group():
4515: 262:                        end_idx = dividers[j].end()
4516: 263:                        segment = html[start_idx:end_idx]
4517: 264:                        meetings.append((segment, m.start(), dividers[j].end()))
4518: 265:                        break
4519: 266:        return meetings
4520: 267: 
4521: 268:    # Load preamble (everything before first divider-block)
4522: 269:    preamble_end = html.find('<div class="divider-block">')
4523: 270:    before = html[:preamble_end]
4524: 271: 
4525: 272:    # Split into per-meeting files
4526: 273:    for i, (segment, start_off, end_off) in enumerate(parse_meetings(html)):
4527: 274:        # Determine meeting folder name from segment
4528: 275:        name_match = re.search(r'class="msg-from">(.+?)</div>', segment[:500])
4529: 276:        if name_match:
4530: 277:            topic = name_match.group(1).strip().lower().replace(' ', '-')
4531: 278:        else:
4532: 279:            topic = f"meeting-{i+1}"
4533: 280:        # Write per-meeting HTML with same preamble
4534: 281:        with open(f"meetings/{topic}/teams-export.html", 'w') as f:
4535: 282:            f.write(before + segment + '\n</div></div></body></html>\n')
4536: 283:    PYEOF
4537: 284:    ```
4538: 285: 
4539: 286: 2. **Filter JSON per meeting.** The full `teams-export.json` contains all meetings concatenated. For each meeting, extract only the JSON messages whose `timestamp` falls between the meeting's start and end:
4540: 287: 
4541: 288:    ```bash
4542: 289:    python3 <<'PYEOF'
4543: 290:    import json
4544: 291:    from datetime import datetime
4545: 292: 
4546: 293:    with open('teams-export.json') as f:
4547: 294:        data = json.load(f)
4548: 295: 
4549: 296:    meetings = [...]  # from ST5 meeting detection
4550: 297:    for m in meetings:
4551: 298:        start_utc = m['start_ts']
4552: 299:        end_utc   = m['end_ts']
4553: 300:        filtered = [
4554: 301:            msg for msg in data
4555: 302:            if msg.get('timestamp', '').startswith(start_utc[:10])
4556: 303:            and start_utc <= msg['timestamp'] <= end_utc
4557: 304:        ]
4558: 305:        with open(f"meetings/{m['folder']}/teams-export.json", 'w') as f:
4559: 306:            json.dump(filtered, f, indent=2)
4560: 307:    PYEOF
4561: 308:    ```
4562: 309: 
4563: 310: 3. **Fix per-meeting HTML metadata.** After splitting, the HTML header still shows the global export counts (total participants, total messages). Update the `#header-row` section in each per-meeting HTML to reflect only that meeting's data:
4564: 311:    - Participant count → distinct participants within the meeting window
4565: 312:    - Message count → filtered JSON message count
4566: 313:    - Date range → meeting start–end dates
4567: 314:    - Title → meeting topic from folder name
4568: 315: 
4569: 316: 4. Write the resulting per-meeting HTML to `<meeting-folder>/teams-export.html`.
4570: 317: 
4571: 318: 5. Write the per-meeting JSON to `<meeting-folder>/teams-export.json`.
4572: 319: 
4573: 320: **Key detail:** The HTML preamble includes embedded CSS styles and a `<script>` block for the compact-view toggle and image modal. These must be preserved in each per-meeting HTML for the file to render correctly standalone.
4574: 321: 
4575: 322: ### ST7: Duration-Label vs Timestamp-Span Correction
4576: 323: 
4577: 324: **Prose:** Correct meeting folder end times to use the greater of the two possible end times.
4578: 325: 
4579: 326: **Steps:**
4580: 327: 
4581: 328: 1. For each meeting, compute two end times:
4582: 329:    - **Timestamp-based:** `Meeting ended` UTC timestamp → IST.
4583: 330:    - **Label-based:** `Meeting started` UTC + `⏱ <duration>` label → IST.
4584: 331: 
4585: 332: 2. Use `max(ts_based, label_based)` as the folder end time.
4586: 333: 
4587: 334: 3. Document the discrepancy in a per-meeting `meeting-notes.yaml` file.
4588: 335: 
4589: 336: **Example discrepancies for the 3 meetings in this export:**
4590: 337: 
4591: 338: | Meeting | TS Span | Label Duration | Delta | Folder End Uses |
4592: 339: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
4593: 340: | Mar 25 intro | 1m 56s | 10m | +8m 04s | Label (10m) |
4594: 341: | May 7 sync | 17m 08s | 20m 38s | +3m 30s | Label (20m38s) |
4595: 342: | Jul 4 staging | 5h 56m 35s | 6h 2m 39s | +6m 04s | Label (6h2m39s) |
4596: 343: 
4597: 344: **Per-meeting `meeting-notes.yaml` (initial, before Phase 5 enrichment):**
4598: 345: 
4599: 346: Rich metadata per meeting:
4600: 347: - `folder_name` — meeting folder path
4601: 348: - `description` — human-readable summary
4602: 349: - `derived_from_work_log` — cross-reference to rough log (file + line + explanation)
4603: 350: - `timestamps` — UTC timestamps (from JSON) plus `duration_label`
4604: 351: - `duration_discrepancy` — ts-based vs label-based duration with delta and note
4605: 352: - `participants` — ordered list (late joiners noted via add-member events)
4606: 353: - `messages` — count of chat messages
4607: 354: - `post_meeting_chat` — structured array of post-meeting messages (speaker, time, content)
4608: 355: - `key_topics` — topic clusters from message content review
4609: 356: 
4610: 357: **Template:**
4611: 358: ```yaml
4612: 359: folder_name: meeting-<date>_<start-HHMMSS>_<end-HHMMSS>-<topic>
4613: 360: description: "<summary>"
4614: 361: derived_from_work_log: |
4615: 362:   <file> line <N>:
4616: 363:   "<excerpt>"
4617: 364:   <match explanation>
4618: 365: 
4619: 366: timestamps:
4620: 367:   meeting_started_utc: "<ISO-8601>"
4621: 368:   meeting_ended_utc: "<ISO-8601>"
4622: 369:   duration_label: "<⏱ value>"
4623: 370: 
4624: 371: duration_discrepancy:
4625: 372:   ts_based: "<H:MM:SS>"
4626: 373:   label_based: "<H:MM:SS>"
4627: 374:   delta: "<H:MM:SS>"
4628: 375:   note: >
4629: 376:     The "⏱ <duration>" label on "Meeting ended" is <delta> longer than the
4630: 377:     actual Meeting started → Meeting ended timestamp span. Folder end time
4631: 378:     uses the greater value (label-based).
4632: 379: 
4633: 380: participants:
4634: 381:   - <name1>
4635: 382:   - <name2>
4636: 383: 
4637: 384: messages: <count>
4638: 385: 
4639: 386: post_meeting_chat:
4640: 387:   entries:
4641: 388:     - speaker: <name>
4642: 389:       time_ist: "<HH:MM>"
4643: 390:       message: "<text>"
4644: 391:   note: "<context>"
4645: 392: 
4646: 393: key_topics:

4648: 395:     detail: "<elaboration or context>"
4649: 396:   - description: "<brief label>"
4650: 397:     detail: "<elaboration or context>"
4651: 398: ```

4742: 489: ## Phase 3: Analyze a Particular Meeting
4743: 490: 
4744: 491: **Prose:** Deep analysis of a specific meeting's HTML content, checking whether the meeting title aligns with the actual chat content.
4745: 492: 
4746: 493: **Steps:**
4747: 494: 
4748: 495: 1. Open the per-meeting HTML file (`teams-export.html`) for the chosen meeting.
4749: 496: 2. Review all messages, attachments, and system events:
4750: 497:    - Message content (text, code snippets)
4751: 498:    - Attachments (files shared, URLs)
4752: 499:    - Participant list and add-member events
4753: 500:    - Duration and recording info
4754: 501: 3. Compare the meeting title against the actual content.
4755: 502: 4. Identify topic clusters present in the conversation.
4756: 503: 
4757: 504: **Example (Jul 4 meeting):** The HTML review revealed 3 distinct topic clusters that the original title `local-testing-environment-setup-for-praveena-razik` did not fully cover:
4758: 505:    1. Local testing env setup — .env files, backend/frontend env URLs
4759: 506:    2. Staging DB dump — SQL dump shared by Dileena, forwarded to Praveena & Razik
4760: 507:    3. API trade processing script — Python code for `API_Pending_Trades` reconciliation
4761: 508: 
4762: 509: This analysis feeds directly into Phase 5 (meeting naming from work logs). The final title was chosen to cover all clusters: `local-testing-env-setup-and-staging-data-reconciliation`.

The pipeline is designed to be applied to any other Teams meeting export file.

4415: 162: ### ST5: Generate Per-Meeting Folders with HTML + JSON
4416: 163: 
4417: 164: **Prose:** Split the full-chat export into per-meeting subfolders. Each subfolder gets a copy of the meeting-specific HTML and JSON from the original export.
4418: 165: 
4419: 166: **Steps:**
4420: 167: 
4421: 168: 1. Parse the JSON file (`teams-export.json`) to identify meeting boundaries.
4422: 169:     - Detect `"Meeting started"` and `"Meeting ended"` system messages from the `messageType` field.
4423: 170:     - Treat `"added <participant>"` messages as pre-meeting context (belongs to the upcoming meeting folder, not a separate meeting).
4424: 171:     - **Meeting vs false-start rule:** A `Meeting started` → `Meeting ended` pair is a real meeting ONLY if it has ≥1 participant message (chat, file share) or a non-zero duration label (`⏱ 10m` etc). A 17-second pair with 0 messages and no label is likely a false start / test. File such meetings under a `.false-starts/` subfolder instead of a `meeting-.../` subfolder. The example in this export (17-second intro with `⏱ 10m` label and 3 messages on Mar 25) IS a real meeting — the label > 0m and messages > 0 are what make it real, not the short duration.
4425: 172: 
4426: 173: 2. For each meeting detected, create a subfolder named:
4427: 174:    ```
4428: 175:    meeting-<YYYY-MM-DD>_<IST-start-HHMMSS>_<IST-end-HHMMSS>-<topic>/
4429: 176:    ```
4430: 177: 
4431: 178: 3. Extract the messages for that meeting from the JSON and write a partial JSON file into the meeting subfolder.
4432: 179: 
4433: 180: **Timestamp computation rules:**
4434: 181: 
4435: 182: - All timestamps in the export are in **UTC** (e.g., `2026-03-25T07:18:11.973Z`).
4436: 183: - Convert to **IST** (+5:30) for folder naming.
4437: 184: - The meeting date used in the folder name is the **IST date** of the meeting start (this matters when meetings start before midnight UTC and span into the next IST day).
4438: 185: - Initial format: `HHMM` (hours+minutes). Later refined to `HHMMSS` (with seconds) in Phase 4.
4439: 186: 
4440: 187: **Duration handling:**
4441: 188: 
4442: 189: - The Teams Chat Exporter places a `⏱ <duration>` label on the "Meeting ended" divider (e.g., `⏱ 10m`, `⏱ 20m 38s`, `⏱ 6h 2m 39s`).
4443: 190: - This label often **differs** from the actual `Meeting started → Meeting ended` timestamp span.
4444: 191: - Initial approach: use the label-based end time as the folder end time (it's always greater).
4445: 192: - **Final rule (ST7):** Folder end time = `max(meeting-ended-timestamp, start + duration-label)`.
4446: 193: 
4447: 194: ### ST6: Split Original HTML at Meeting Boundaries
4448: 195: 
4449: 196: **IMPORTANT REFINEMENT:** The initial approach split meetings by generating partial HTML from JSON. This produced minimal HTML missing the rich content (embedded images, proper CSS, participant avatars, divider styling). The session then switched to **splitting the original HTML file** at meeting boundaries.
4450: 197: 
4451: 198: **HTML structure overview:**
4452: 199: 
4453: 200: The Teams Chat Exporter HTML has this overall structure:
4454: 201: ```html
4455: 202: <html>
4456: 203:   <head>
4457: 204:     <style>...</style>        <!-- CSS for the entire export -->
4458: 205:     <script>...</script>      <!-- compact-view toggle, image modal -->
4459: 206:   </head>
4460: 207:   <body>
4461: 208:     <div id="wrapper">
4462: 209:       <div id="header-row">...</div>         <!-- global header (title, counts) -->
4463: 210:       <div id="export-body">
4464: 211:         <div class="divider-block">          <!-- Meeting started -->
4465: 212:           <div class="divider-left">
4466: 213:             <div class="msg-from">Meeting started</div>
4467: 214:             <div class="msg-timestamp" datetime="2026-...">...</div>
4468: 215:           </div>
4469: 216:         </div>
4470: 217:         ... message rows ...
4471: 218:         <div class="divider-block">          <!-- Meeting ended -->
4472: 219:           <div class="divider-left">
4473: 220:             <span class="msg-timestamp" datetime="...">⏱ 10m</span>
4474: 221:             <div class="msg-from">Meeting ended</div>
4475: 222:           </div>
4476: 223:         </div>
4477: 224:         ... post-meeting messages ...
4478: 225:         <div class="divider-block">          <!-- next Meeting started -->
4479: 226:           ...
4480: 227:         </div>
4481: 228:       </div>
4482: 229:     </div>
4483: 230:   </body>
4484: 231: </html>
4485: 232: ```
4486: 233: 
4487: 234: **Divider block closing pattern varies by export version.** The closing `</div>` count after a `<div class="divider-block">` depends on nesting depth. Instead of counting closing tags, use a split-on-content approach (see script below).
4488: 235: 
4489: 236: **Steps:**
4490: 237: 
4491: 238: 1. **Split HTML by meeting boundaries** using a pattern-matching script (not hardcoded byte offsets which break on different exports):
4492: 239: 
4493: 240:    ```bash
4494: 241:    python3 <<'PYEOF'
4495: 242:    import re, os, json
4496: 243:    from datetime import datetime, timezone, timedelta
4497: 244: 
4498: 245:    IST = timezone(timedelta(hours=5, minutes=30))
4499: 246:    LATEST_FOLDER = None  # set to latest exporter folder
4500: 247: 
4501: 248:    def parse_meetings(html):
4502: 249:        # Find every divider block
4503: 250:        dividers = list(re.finditer(
4504: 251:            r'<div class="divider-block">(.*?)</div>\s*</div>\s*</div>',
4505: 252:            html, re.DOTALL
4506: 253:        ))
4507: 254:        meetings = []
4508: 255:        for i, m in enumerate(dividers):
4509: 256:            block = m.group()
4510: 257:            if 'Meeting started' in block:
4511: 258:                start_idx = m.start()
4512: 259:                # Find the next Meeting ended divider
4513: 260:                for j in range(i+1, len(dividers)):
4514: 261:                    if 'Meeting ended' in dividers[j].group():
4515: 262:                        end_idx = dividers[j].end()
4516: 263:                        segment = html[start_idx:end_idx]
4517: 264:                        meetings.append((segment, m.start(), dividers[j].end()))
4518: 265:                        break
4519: 266:        return meetings

8343: 5518: # Skill: git-atomic-commit-construction
8344: 5519: 
8345: 5520: # Git Atomic Commit Construction Skill
8346: 5521: 
8347: 5522: > **Skill ID:** `git-atomic-commit-construction`

8351: 5526: ## Description
8352: 5527: 
8353: 5528: Construct high-quality, atomic Git commits from a set of working-tree
8354: 5529: changes. This skill covers the full lifecycle: environment validation,
8355: 5530: change analysis, logical grouping, hunk-based staging, formatting
8356: 5531: isolation, commit message quality, execution with user authorization,
8357: 5532: and post-commit verification.
8358: 5533: 
8359: 5534: Every commit produced by this skill is independent, logically coherent,
8360: 5535: and buildable. Mixed concerns are never committed together. Formatting
8361: 5536: is separated from logic. Configuration is coupled to its functional
8362: 5537: change. The user retains full control via mandatory preview and explicit
8363: 5538: "start" authorization.
8364: 5539: 
8365: 5540: ## Source Rules
8366: 5541: 
8367: 5542: This skill distills and operationalizes the following rule files:
8368: 5543: 
8369: 5544: | Rule File | Scope Incorporated |
8370: 5545: |---|---|
8371: 5546: | [`git-atomic-commit-construction-rules.md`](../../../ai-agent-rules/git-atomic-commit-construction-rules.md) | All 15 phases (primary source) |
8372: 5547: | [`git-operation-rules.md`](../../../ai-agent-rules/git-operation-rules.md) | Phase -1, 0, 1 (environment, repo context, change detection) and Sections 2–4 (commit/push/stash protocols) |
8373: 5548: 
8374: 5549: For history refinement (splitting existing commits), see the
8375: 5550: [`git_history_refinement`](../git-history-refinement/SKILL.md) skill.
8376: 5551: For complex multi-branch rebasing, see the

8380: 5555: 
8381: 5556: | Requirement | Minimum |
8382: 5557: |---|---|
8383: 5558: | VCS | Git 2.x+ |
8384: 5559: | Shell | PowerShell 5.1+ or Bash 4+ |

8387: 5562: 
8388: 5563: ## When to Apply
8389: 5564: 
8390: 5565: Apply this skill when:
8391: 5566: 
8392: 5567: - A user asks to "commit changes," "arrange commits," or "stage and commit"
8393: 5568: - `git status` shows staged, unstaged, or untracked modifications
8394: 5569: - Multiple unrelated changes exist in the working tree and need separation
8395: 5570: - A user asks to review what should be committed
8396: 5571: - **After ANY submodule commit is executed, the skill AUTOMATICALLY checks for
8397: 5572:   and offers the parent repository submodule SHA update (if applicable) and
8398: 5573:   executes it upon user "yes" — no separate user request needed**
8399: 5574: 
8400: 5575: Do NOT apply when:
8401: 5576: 
8402: 5577: - The user asks to refine or split **existing** commits — use
8403: 5578:   [`git_history_refinement`](../git-history-refinement/SKILL.md) instead
8404: 5579: - The user asks to rebase branches — use
8405: 5580:   [`git_rebase`](../git-rebase-standardization/SKILL.md) instead
8406: 5581: - The request is a simple single-file, single-concern commit with no
8407: 5582:   mixed changes (a lightweight commit suffices without the full protocol)
8408: 5583: - The files being committed are **personal-only** and should NOT reach the
8409: 5584:   team's `origin` — route the commit to a personal sandbox branch via
8410: 5585:   [`git-personal-sandbox-remote`](../git-personal-sandbox-remote/SKILL.md)
8411: 5586:   (this skill still applies to the commit itself, but the destination
8412: 5587:   remote/branch changes)
8413: 5588: 
8414: 5589: **Push Policy (GLOBAL)**: The agent MUST NEVER execute `git push` automatically.
8415: 5590: After any commit(s), the agent MAY OFFER to push (e.g., "Push to remote?") but
8416: 5591: MUST WAIT for explicit user approval. Only push when the user explicitly says
8417: 5592: "yes", "push", or issues a direct `git push` command. No exceptions.
8418: 5593: 
8419: 5594: ---
8420: 5595: 
8421: 5596: ## Step-by-Step Procedure
8422: 5597: 
8423: 5598: ### Step 0 — Environment & Repository Context
8424: 5599: 
8425: 5600: Before any Git commands, validate the environment and establish context.
8426: 5601: 
8427: 5602: #### 0a — Authenticate Services
8428: 5603: 
8429: 5604: Verify authentication for required services:
8430: 5605: 
8431: 5606: ```powershell
8432: 5607: gh auth status        # GitHub CLI
8433: 5608: ```
8434: 5609: 
8435: 5610: If authentication is missing, guide the user through login.
8436: 5611: 
8437: 5612: #### 0b — Identify the Target Repository
8438: 5613: 
8439: 5614: Determine the correct repository from the user's request and file paths.
8440: 5615: 
8441: 5616: - **Nested repositories:** If changes are in a sub-directory that is its
8442: 5617:   own Git project, use `PAGER=cat git -C` to execute `PAGER=cat git` commands in that repository.
8443: 5618: - **Ambiguity:** If multiple repositories exist in the workspace and the
8444: 5619:   target is unclear, ask the user for clarification.
8445: 5620: 
8446: 5621: #### 0c — Working Directory Persistence (Critical)
8447: 5622: 
8448: 5623: When working with `git` commands, use `git -C <path>` for reliable directory targeting:
8449: 5624: 
8450: 5625: ```powershell
8451: 5626: # Recommended: git -C with absolute path
8452: 5627: git -C /path/to/repo status
8453: 5628: git -C /path/to/repo diff HEAD
8454: 5629: 
8455: 5630: # Why this matters: Shell `cd` commands do not persist across tool invocations
8456: 5631: # in stateless execution environments. Using git -C ensures consistent behavior
8457: 5632: # across all command chains and multi-step workflows.
8458: 5633: 
8459: 5634: # Pattern for multi-repo work:
8460: 5635: git -C /repo1 status
8461: 5636: git -C /repo2 status
8462: 5637: git -C /repo1 add file.txt
8463: 5638: ```
8464: 5639: 
8465: 5640: **When `cd` alone is insufficient:**
8466: 5641: 
8467: 5642: - In tools/environments where `cd` doesn't persist state across invocations
8468: 5643: - When working with multiple repositories in sequence
8469: 5644: - For clarity in tool-generated scripts and audit trails
8470: 5645: 
8471: 5646: **Legacy pattern (avoid):**
8472: 5647: 
8473: 5648: ```powershell
8474: 5649: # ❌ May not reliably persist across invocations
8475: 5650: cd /path/to/repo; git status
8476: 5651: ```
8477: 5652: 
8478: 5653: **Preferred pattern:**
8479: 5654: 
8480: 5655: ```powershell
8481: 5656: # ✅ Reliable and explicit
8482: 5657: git -C /path/to/repo status
8483: 5658: ```
8484: 5659: 
8485: 5660: #### 0d — Verify Build Tool Permissions
8486: 5661: 
8487: 5662: Ensure build tools have execute permissions:
8488: 5663: 
8489: 5664: ```bash
8490: 5665: chmod +x gradlew      # Gradle wrapper example
8491: 5666: ```
8492: 5667: 
8493: 5668: #### 0e — Active Branch Verification (Critical)
8494: 5669: 
8495: 5670: The agent MUST ensure the repository is not in a "detached HEAD" state before committing.
8496: 5671: 
8497: 5672: 1. **Check Current Branch**: Run `git branch --show-current`.
8498: 5673: 2. **Handle Detached HEAD**: If the output is empty (detached HEAD), the agent MUST
8499: 5674:    identify and checkout the appropriate branch (usually the default branch,
8500: 5675:    e.g., `main`) before proceeding.
8501: 5676: 3. **Upstream Alignment**: Run `git pull` to synchronize with the remote and avoid push-time conflicts.
8502: 5677: 
8503: 5678: #### 0f — Pre-Edit Repo Role Classification (Critical for unfamiliar repos)
8504: 5679: 
8505: 5680: When the upcoming commit touches files in a repository this session has not
8506: 5681: previously edited — especially when two cloned-locally repos share a name
8507: 5682: prefix or suffix — invoke the
8508: 5683: [`canonical-source-vs-workflow-repo-audit`](../canonical-source-vs-workflow-repo-audit/SKILL.md)
8509: 5684: audit BEFORE the first edit:
8510: 5685: 
8511: 5686: ```bash
8512: 5687: python3 .agents/skills/canonical-source-vs-workflow-repo-audit/scripts/audit-repo-role.py /path/to/file
8513: 5688: ```
8514: 5689: 
8515: 5690: If the verdict is `workflow` or `mirror`, STOP and locate the canonical
8516: 5691: source repo. If the verdict is `unknown`, ask the user. Skipping this
8517: 5692: audit risks landing the work in a repo whose changes never reach the
8518: 5693: canonical artifact (real-world precedent: Account-Ledger-Server vs
8519: 5694: Account-Ledger-Server-PHP, May 2026)
8520: 5695: 
8521: 5696: ---
8522: 5697: 
8523: 5698: ### Step 1 — Deep Change Analysis
8524: 5699: 
8525: 5700: Perform a dependency analysis of ALL modifications before staging
8526: 5701: anything.
8527: 5702: 
8528: 5703: #### 1a — Detect All Changes
8529: 5704: 
8530: 5705: Use `git status` to discover staged, unstaged, and untracked changes:
8531: 5706: 
8532: 5707: ```powershell
8533: 5708: git status
8534: 5709: ```
8535: 5710: 
8536: 5711: **Complete Scope (Critical):** The analysis MUST cover ALL three change
8537: 5712: categories — **staged**, **unstaged**, AND **untracked** — as a single
8538: 5713: unified inventory from the very first step. Untracked files are
8539: 5714: first-class members of the change scope, not a secondary check.
8540: 5715: Failing to include untracked files in the initial analysis leads to
8541: 5716: incomplete commit plans and files discovered only after execution.
8542: 5717: 
8543: 5718: **Untracked files:** Any untracked file not excluded by `.gitignore` is
8544: 5719: a candidate for version control. The agent **MUST NOT** stage untracked
8545: 5720: files without explicit user confirmation to avoid committing credentials,
8546: 5721: large binaries, or environment-specific files. When an untracked file's
8547: 5722: origin is unclear (cross-repo scratch, tool dump, captured diff), invoke
8548: 5723: the [`untracked-scratch-triage`](../untracked-scratch-triage/SKILL.md)
8549: 5724: skill to classify and dispose of it before continuing the inventory.
8550: 5725: 
8551: 5726: #### 1b — Use `git ls-files` as Source of Truth
8552: 5727: 
8553: 5728: For rename or restructuring operations, `git ls-files` is the
8554: 5729: authoritative list of tracked files — not `Get-ChildItem` or `find`,
8555: 5730: which include git-ignored content:
8556: 5731: 
8557: 5732: ```powershell
8558: 5733: git ls-files
8559: 5734: ```
8560: 5735: 
8561: 5736: #### 1c — Read `.gitignore` for Tracked vs Ignored
8562: 5737: 
8563: 5738: Read `.gitignore` carefully, paying special attention to **negation
8564: 5739: patterns** (`!`) that re-include specific files inside ignored
8565: 5740: directories:
8566: 5741: 
8567: 5742: ```gitignore
8568: 5743: # Example: directory ignored, but .zip files are tracked
8569: 5744: pevers/*
8570: 5745: !pevers/*.zip
8571: 5746: ```
8572: 5747: 
8573: 5748: #### 1d — Analyze Change Dependencies
8574: 5749: 
8575: 5750: - **Shared Identifiers:** Group changes that modify the same functions,
8576: 5751:   classes, or constants across different files.
8577: 5752: - **Cross-File References:** If file A depends on a change in file B
8578: 5753:   (e.g., an import, a link, a `.gitignore` pattern), they MUST be in
8579: 5754:   the same atomic commit.
8580: 5755: - **Categorical Alignment:** Group changes by architectural layer (UI,
8581: 5756:   Logic, Docs) unless they are functionally coupled.
8582: 5757: 
8583: 5758: #### 1e — Workflow-First Priority
8584: 5759: 
8585: 5760: If changes involve CI/CD workflows (GitHub Actions, scripts), the agent
8586: 5761: **MUST** fix, test, and verify workflow functionality **BEFORE** arranging
8587: 5762: or executing commits. Pipeline stability takes precedence over
8588: 5763: documentation or stylistic refinements.
8589: 5764: 
8590: 5765: #### 1f — Present Complete Inventory
8591: 5766: 
8592: 5767: List **ALL changes** — staged, unstaged, AND untracked (not just
8593: 5768: violations or modifications to already-tracked files) — with their
8594: 5769: status. This gives the user full visibility and ensures no file is
8595: 5770: analyzed as an afterthought:
8596: 5771: 
8597: 5772: | # | File | Status | Action |
8598: 5773: |---|---|---|---|
8599: 5774: | 1 | `.gitignore` | Modified | 🔄 Update |

8601: 5776: | 3 | `README.md` | Untracked | ❓ Confirm with user |

8605: 5780: ### 1g — Redaction Pre-Check (Sensitive Content Audit)
8606: 5781: 
8607: 5782: Before any staging or logical grouping, audit all **new/untracked** and
8608: 5783: **modified** files for content that must be redacted per the
8609: 5784: [redaction-portability](../redaction-portability/SKILL.md) skill — especially
8610: 5785: prose-heavy files like skill `SKILL.md`, rule docs, and conversation logs.
8611: 5786: 
8612: 5787: **Scan for:**
8613: 5788: 
8614: 5789: 1. **Organization-specific Jira ticket IDs** (e.g., `PROJ-1234`) — replace with
8615: 5790:    `<TICKET-ID>` or `<TICKET-ID-PROJ>`.
8616: 5791: 2. **Internal repository URLs** (e.g., `github.com/<org>/<repo>`) — replace
8617: 5792:    `<org>/<repo>` with `<ORG>/<REPO>`.
8618: 5793: 3. **Cross-repo relative links** — `../` chains that escape the current repo's
8619: 5794:    root into a sibling directory (no `.gitmodules` registration). Run the
8620: 5795:    [detect-cross-repo-links.py](../redaction-portability/scripts/detect-cross-repo-links.py)
8621: 5796:    script from the redaction-portability skill.
8622: 5797: 4. **Literal organization names, internal codenames, hostnames, and usernames**
8623: 5798:    in prose — replace with canonical placeholders (`<corp>`, `<author>`, etc.).
8624: 5799: 5. **Project-specific skill names / paths** in base-published skills (e.g., a
8625: 5800:    composer row in a base skill referencing a project-specific skill in a
8626: 5801:    different repo).
8627: 5802: 
8628: 5803: **When to run this audit:**
8629: 5804: 
8630: 5805: - **Immediately after Step 1f** (Complete Inventory) — you have the full file
8631: 5806:   list, and no work has been wasted on grouping or staging content that will
8632: 5807:   need post-hoc redaction.
8633: 5808: - **Any time a new file is added** to the working tree mid-session (e.g.,
8634: 5809:   skill-factory generation, conversation export).
8635: 5810: 
8636: 5811: **Remediation workflow:**
8637: 5812: 
8638: 5813: 1. Read each flagged file, identify the violating strings.
8639: 5814: 2. Apply canonical placeholders per
8640: 5815:    [redaction-portability §2](../redaction-portability/SKILL.md#2-canonical-placeholder-vocabulary).
8641: 5816: 3. If the violation is a cross-repo link: either delete the link entirely or
8642: 5817:    replace with a name-only reference (see redaction-portability repair rules).
8643: 5818: 4. Re-run the audit to confirm zero remaining violations.
8644: 5819: 5. Only then proceed to Step 2 (Logical Grouping).
8645: 5820: 
8646: 5821: The redaction-portability skill **MUST** be cited as a dependency in any commit
8647: 5822: that touches skill or rule files, so downstream tooling knows to invoke the
8648: 5823: same audit.
8649: 5824:

8651: 5826: 
8652: 5827: ### Step 2 — Logical Grouping (Arrangement)
8653: 5828: 
8654: 5829: Arrange detected changes into a proposed sequence of commits.
8655: 5830: 
8656: 5831: #### 2a — Independence Principle
8657: 5832: 
8658: 5833: Each commit must stand alone. If the repository were checked out at
8659: 5834: that commit, it should still build/function (or be logically coherent).
8660: 5835: 
8661: 5836: #### 2b — Atomic Principle
8662: 5837: 
8663: 5838: Never commit half of a logical change. If a file contains two unrelated
8664: 5839: changes, use **hunk-based staging** (Step 3).
8665: 5840: 
8666: 5841: #### 2c — Buildable State Priority
8667: 5842: 
8668: 5843: While atomicity is the goal, maintaining a buildable repository takes
8669: 5844: precedence. If a core infrastructure change (e.g., a signature change in
8670: 5845: a shared helper) breaks all consumers, the refactor and the resulting
8671: 5846: fixes in consumer files MUST be consolidated into a single commit.
8672: 5847: 
8673: 5848: #### 2d — The Commit Preview (Mandatory Verbose Display)
8674: 5849: 
8675: 5850: Present the proposed "Arranged Commits" using a structured format with
8676: 5851: **maximum detail**. For files with mixed concerns requiring hunk-based
8677: 5852: staging, the preview **MUST** include the specific git hunks.
8678: 5853: 
8679: 5854: **Mandates for writing the preview:**
8680: 5855: 
8681: 5856: 1. **`@@` Header Verification** — Before writing any `@@ -N,M +N,M @@` line,
8682: 5857:    run `git diff --unified=3 -- <file>` and copy the exact range header from
8683: 5858:    the actual output. Never estimate or compute from memory — wrong headers
8684: 5859:    make the preview useless for verification.
8685: 5860: 
8686: 5861: 2. **Fence Collision Handling** — When a diff hunk contains lines that are
8687: 5862:    themselves triple-backtick fenced code blocks (` ```text`, ` ```bash`,
8688: 5863:    and their closing ` ``` `), wrap the diff in **`~~~diff`** / **`~~~`**
8689: 5864:    instead of ` ```diff ` / ` ``` `. Backtick fences inside a backtick-fenced
8690: 5865:    block terminate the outer block prematurely, breaking the markdown preview.
8691: 5866:    The tilde fence (`~~~`) is only closed by another `~~~`, so inner backtick
8692: 5867:    blocks survive as literal content.
8693: 5868: 
8694: 5869: 3. **No Content Truncation** — All hunks MUST be shown in full. Lines of
8695: 5870:    context MUST NOT be replaced with `...` or any other truncation marker.
8696: 5871:    If the combined diff is too large for one conversation message, split the
8697: 5872:    preview across batches ($2g) and present one batch at a time.
8698: 5873: 
8699: 5874: 4. **Preview Artifact** — Write the full preview to
8700: 5875:    `scratch/commit-preview.md` (use
8701: 5876:    [`repo-scratch-output-capture`](../repo-scratch-output-capture/SKILL.md)
8702: 5877:    to ensure `scratch/` exists and is gitignored). The user can then refer to
8703: 5878:    specific line numbers when giving feedback. Present the summary in the
8704: 5879:    conversation as well.
8705: 5880: 
8706: 5881: Template:
8707: 5882: 
8708: 5883: ````markdown
8709: 5884: ## Arranged Commits Preview
8710: 5885: 
8711: 5886: ### Commit 1: [type](scope): [title]
8712: 5887: - **Files**: [file1.md], [file2.md]
8713: 5888: - **Message**:
8714: 5889:   ```
8715: 5890:   [type](scope): [title]
8716: 5891: 
8717: 5892:   [Body line 1]
8718: 5893:   [Body line 2]
8719: 5894:   ```
8720: 5895: - **Hunks/Preview**:
8721: 5896:   ```diff
8722: 5897:   [Show actual hunks for this commit — use ~~~diff/~~~ if hunks contain ```
8723: 5898:   ]
8724: 5899:   ```
8725: 5900: 
8726: 5901: ### Commit 2: [type](scope): [title]
8727: 5902: - **Files**: [file3.md]
8728: 5903: - **Message**:
8729: 5904:   ```
8730: 5905:   [type](scope): [title]
8731: 5906: 
8732: 5907:   [Body line 1]
8733: 5908:   ```
8734: 5909: ---
8735: 5910: Please say "start" to begin the sequential execution of these atomic
8736: 5911: commits.
8737: 5912: ````
8738: 5913: 
8739: 5914: #### 2d.1 — Iterative Preview Fixup
8740: 5915: 
8741: 5916: After presenting the commit preview, the user may give feedback by line
8742: 5917: number (e.g., "check line 98 — still broken"). Feedbacks typically
8743: 5918: point to one of these issues in the preview:
8744: 5919: 
8745: 5920: - Wrong `@@` header (fix by verifying against actual `git diff`)
8746: 5921: - Truncated content with `...` (restore full hunk)
8747: 5922: - Nested fenced code blocks breaking markdown (switch to `~~~diff`/`~~~`)
8748: 5923: - Missing context lines around changes (include the default 3-line context)
8749: 5924: 
8750: 5925: Fix, re-write the preview to `scratch/commit-preview.md`, and re-present.
8751: 5926: Loop until the user confirms the preview is correct. Do NOT begin execution
8752: 5927: until the user says "start".

8754: 5929: #### 2e — Commit Authorization
8755: 5930:

8770: 5945: - **Submodule syncs**: `.gitmodules` URL change and any root `AGENTS.md` row
8771: 5946:   referencing the submodule → same commit as the submodule pointer advance.
8772: 5947: - **Any artifact with a shared index entry**: treat the index row as part of the
8773: 5948:   artifact's definition, not as metadata to collect last.
